output.name: Tesuk — The Counting Hands (The Spindle)
output.myth: Hesk wound every string the islands flew, and she kept count of each knot in her two hands. When Aun cut the string and the sky drifted off, she did not stop counting. Her drop spindle slipped and went up after the cut end, still turning. That is Hasket, a fist and a half south-east, and the thread she was spinning to hold the sky close still runs from it. Aun flew like Kisal to the west, the tailless kite Ennu makes for children who do not yet know the wind. She held her hands open so the knots would not slip, and she counts them still. Each knot is a fisherman, a child, a kite that flew too far. My grandmother said the count is wrong by one. Hesk knows which one. She will not say, because it is the knot Aun tied in his own string before he cut it. He is still out there, trying to be counted. Tavo laughs at her and cannot be bargained with. Sil looks for him in the same dark. Mend your net. Count your knots. Keep your palms open.
output.finding: Start at Sathun, the Lidded Jar, and sight one hand-span (about 18°) straight south across the sky, where Tesuk is the next group of stars you reach.
